title: Quantization Gateway Recommender — scoring & spreadsheet draft
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for a lightweight decision engine — the "Quantization Gateway Recommender" — plus a companion spreadsheet layout that ops/product teams can use to recommend model-quantization variants (FP16/FP8/INT8/4-bit) by balancing cost, latency, and quality. The goal: give engineers a repeatable, tunable scoring function and a simple sensitivity-sweep plan that produces recommended routing splits for traffic and a small set of tuned defaults for Redwood Optimize.

Summary / Thesis:
- Many customers want to save inference costs by quantizing models but need automated, defensible guidance for which quantization level to use and how to route traffic.
- We propose a composite scoring approach with three normalized axes (cost, latency, quality penalty) and a single user-facing knob called "gamma" that controls tolerance to quality degradation.
- The companion spreadsheet (structure below) will support per-variant benchmarking as input and then output a ranked list plus traffic-share recommendations (softmax-based).

Background and constraints:
- Inputs available from bench tests: p50/p95 latency (ms), tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens (USD), and one or more quality deltas (BLEU/ROUGE/perplexity or model-specific eval score).
- Product requirements that influence weighting: latency SLOs (e.g., p50 <= 120ms), cost reduction targets, and maximum acceptable quality regression (e.g., <= 2% average metric drop).
- Must be simple enough to run in a spreadsheet and also translatable into a backend rule for Redwood Optimize.

Scoring proposal (high level):
We compute three normalized scores (lower is better):
- cost_score = cost_per_1k / cost_baseline
- latency_score = p50_latency_ms / p50_baseline_latency_ms
- quality_penalty = 1 + (quality_loss_pct * quality_sensitivity)  // quality_loss_pct expressed as absolute pct points, positive when worse

Composite score = w_cost * cost_score + w_latency * latency_score + w_quality * quality_penalty

Where "gamma" maps to quality_sensitivity:
- conservative (gamma = 0.3) -> quality_sensitivity = 2.0
- balanced (gamma = 1.0) -> quality_sensitivity = 1.0
- aggressive (gamma = 2.5) -> quality_sensitivity = 0.4

Default weights (starting point): w_cost=0.5, w_latency=0.3, w_quality=0.2. These are tunable per-customer; we store defaults in the workspace.

Why this shape?
- Cost and latency are normalized to the baseline so we can reason about relative wins.
- Quality penalty is multiplicative (1 + delta * sensitivity) because even a small regression should have exponentially worse impact in conservative settings.
- Single knob (gamma) makes product exposure simple: increase gamma to prioritize quality more.

Spreadsheet layout (recommended tabs and columns):
- Tab 1: raw-benchmarks (one row per variant)
  Columns: variant, model_version, quant_level, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, cost_per_1k_usd, quality_metric_name, quality_baseline_value, quality_variant_value, quality_loss_pct
  Example formula hints (Google Sheets):
    - quality_loss_pct = (quality_variant_value - quality_baseline_value) / quality_baseline_value * 100
    - normalized_cost = cost_per_1k_usd / INDEX(cost_per_1k_usd, MATCH("baseline", quant_level_range, 0))
    - normalized_latency = p50_latency_ms / p50_baseline_latency_ms
- Tab 2: scoring-config
  Columns (single-row config): baseline_variant, w_cost, w_latency, w_quality, gamma_label, quality_sensitivity
- Tab 3: scored-variants (computed)
  Columns: variant, normalized_cost, normalized_latency, quality_penalty, composite_score, rank
  Example composite_score formula (sheet): = w_cost*normalized_cost + w_latency*normalized_latency + w_quality*quality_penalty
- Tab 4: routing-recommendation
  Inputs: temperature (T), mapping from score->traffic (softmax)
  Formula for traffic_share (pseudo): softmax_input = -composite_score / T; traffic_share = exp(softmax_input) / SUM(exp(softmax_input_range))
- Tab 5: sensitivity-sweeps (gamma sweep table)
  Columns: gamma_value, selected_variant (min composite_score), top2_split (traffic %), estimated_cost_savings_pct, estimated_quality_risk_pct

Sample numbers (illustrative):
- Baseline: FP16 (baseline): p50 = 120 ms, cost_per_1k = $0.12, quality_loss_pct = 0.0
- FP8: p50 = 95 ms, cost_per_1k = $0.08, quality_loss_pct = 0.5
- INT8: p50 = 85 ms, cost_per_1k = $0.07, quality_loss_pct = 1.8
- 4-bit: p50 = 70 ms, cost_per_1k = $0.05, quality_loss_pct = 4.5

Using defaults (w_cost=0.5, w_latency=0.3, w_quality=0.2) and gamma=1.0 (quality_sensitivity=1.0):
  normalized_costs = [1.0, 0.667, 0.583, 0.417]
  normalized_latencies = [1.0, 0.792, 0.708, 0.583]
  quality_penalties = [1.0, 1.005, 1.018, 1.045]
  composite_scores ~= [0.5*1 + 0.3*1 + 0.2*1, 0.5*0.667 + 0.3*0.792 + 0.2*1.005, ...]
  numeric example:
    FP16 -> 1.0
    FP8  -> 0.5*0.667 + 0.3*0.792 + 0.2*1.005 = 0.3335 + 0.2376 + 0.201 = 0.7721
    INT8 -> 0.5*0.583 + 0.3*0.708 + 0.2*1.018 = 0.2915 + 0.2124 + 0.2036 = 0.7075
    4-bit-> 0.5*0.417 + 0.3*0.583 + 0.2*1.045 = 0.2085 + 0.1749 + 0.209 = 0.5924
  Ranking (lower is better): 4-bit, INT8, FP8, FP16 (note: this toy example shows cost/latency wins may push aggressive quantized variants to top even with quality penalty; gamma & w_quality will reverse this for conservative customers)

Mapping to traffic (softmax):
- Use negative composite_score because lower is better. With temperature T=0.02 we get sharper allocations (can be tuned). This gives per-variant traffic_pct recommendations. For safety, add hard rules: do not allocate >X% to any variant if quality_loss_pct > Y (configurable). Example safety defaults: max_for_loss_>2% = 10% (can be tuned).

Sensitivity sweep plan (spreadsheet + runbook):
1) Gather bench CSVs for each candidate variant (p50,p95,tokens/cost, eval metrics).
2) Populate Tab 1 and check baseline alignment.
3) Run gamma sweep: gamma values = [0.3, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.5]; capture top variant and estimated cost savings.
4) Produce a short 1-page summary with recommended default gamma and suggested A/B canary routing percentages for staged rollouts.
5) For customers with strict quality SLOs, run per-prompt-set evals and use a stricter quality_sensitivity (gamma >= 1.5).

Operational safety checklist (for any auto-recommendation):
- Have a canary with 1–5% traffic for any variant with quality_loss_pct > 1.0
- p95 latency must not exceed SLO + 20% for any recommended variant
- Monitor per-prompt quality metrics and auto-rollback if degradation > configured threshold within first 10k requests

Integration notes for Redwood Optimize console/API:
- Expose gamma as a slider: Conservative/Balanced/Aggressive mapped to discrete quality_sensitivity values.
- Show two charts: Cost vs Quality tradeoff curve and per-gamma recommended routing splits.
- Backend API: POST /v1/optimize/quant-gateway/recommend {bench_csv_url, baseline_variant, gamma, temperature, safety_config} -> returns scored_variants + traffic_splits + diagnostics.
- Store config per-customer with audit trail (who changed gamma, when).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How to combine multiple quality metrics (ROUGE vs perplexity vs human A/B)? Proposed: normalize each to baseline and combine with metric-specific weights; include a composite "quality_index" column in the spreadsheet.
- Should the quality_penalty be additive instead of multiplicative in certain regimes? (A/B needed.)
- Default safety thresholds (quality_loss_pct cutoffs and max_traffic_for_high_loss) need product & SRE alignment.

Next steps (owner + ETA):
- Aisha: build initial Google Sheet (tabs above) and populate with existing bench data (due 2026-02-28)
- Marco: prototype backend scoring endpoint and softmax mapper (PR in repo) (due 2026-03-10)
- Claire: design console slider and charts (mockups) (due 2026-03-05)
- Diego: define SRE safety gate config and rollback rules (due 2026-03-12)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight and opinionated — the goal is an actionable spreadsheet + a single-knob UX for teams. Please comment on weighting defaults and suggested safety thresholds.

Attachments & quick links: bench CSVs in internal bucket (see linked_artifacts), related PR #412, Jira PRODOPT-238.

End of draft.
